concept.title: overview
concept.shortdesc: A docs platform where "which release applies" and "who may see this" are one rule, written once in the content and applied everywhere it is shown.

conbody.p: Authors write DITA in a Git repository. The build compiles it into a release snapshot that keeps every element's applicability, and each reader is served only what their release and entitlements allow: on the docs site, in the help panel inside your apps, in search, and in PDF manuals.

section.title: One rule for release and entitlement
section.p: Most documentation tools filter by release when they build, then handle access in a separate layer, if at all. In , any map entry, topic or element can carry standard DITA filtering attributes, and one filter decides both questions:

ul.li: product and feature are matched against what the reader's organization is entitled to.
release takes version ranges, such as 0.1.., and is matched against the release the reader runs.
audience, platform and the other DITA attributes are filtered once, at build time, with a DITAVAL file.

fig.title: Every output goes through the same filtered view

image.alt: Diagram: DITA source with product, release and audience attributes goes through the build-time DITAVAL into a release snapshot that keeps its conditions. The reader filter turns the snapshot into one view that feeds navigation, pages, search, the help panel and PDF publications.

section.p: The filter is fail-closed and never leaks through links, titles or search: a link to a page the reader cannot see renders as plain text, and a hidden page answers with the same 404 as a missing one. See .

section.title: Architecture
section.p: The same packages run on an author's laptop and on the server, so what an author previews is what readers get.

ul.li: Locally, the command validates a docs project, previews it as any reader, and prints PDF publications.

Hosted, a push to the docs repository fires a GitHub webhook. A worker builds and validates the commit, and the web service serves signed-in readers their filtered pages. A push that fails validation never goes live.
In your apps, a small widget opens a help panel on the topic for the current screen, filtered for the signed-in user.

fig.title: The hosted platform: web, worker, Postgres and a blob store

image.alt: Diagram: the docs repository sends a push webhook to the web service, which queues a job in Postgres. The worker fetches the commit, builds and validates it, stores assets in the blob store and publishes the release to Postgres. Readers and host apps are served by the web service through the reader filter.

section.title: What release includes

ul.li: The build and filter core, the opend CLI and a local previewer.
The hosted path: push to publish, OIDC reader sign-in, filtered delivery and an admin API.
Context-sensitive help embedded in your own web apps.
PDF publications from bookmaps, filtered per reader.

section.p: The web editor, site-wide search on the docs site and multi-tenancy come later and reuse the same packages. See .
